title: What a payments internship teaches you that a LeetCode streak cannot
subtitle: Practice problems prove you can solve puzzles. Systems that move money teach you to ask what happens when things go wrong twice.

publication.name: Level Up Coding
publication.pitch: This piece argues that owning an unglamorous payments system teaches three engineering habits (idempotency, append-only ledgers and reconciliation) that make stronger interview evidence than practice-problem streaks. It mixes a concrete engineering explainer, with links to Stripe's and Airbnb's own write-ups, with practical advice for students describing their internship work in interviews. Please check it against your current submission guidelines; I am happy to adjust length or tags.

cover_image.alt: A card payment terminal on a shop counter, waiting for a customer to tap their card.

seo_description: Idempotency, ledgers and reconciliation: the habits a payments internship builds, and how to turn them into a strong interview answer.
